title: The handover, spread
summary: The handover you approved in round 4, with the clutter taken out of the drawing (no title-block boxes, no handover-test line, no row labels, a quieter key) and a small detail card that opens beside each document when you hover, tab to or tap it.
story: This is the payoff: the six problems from the founder's letter are struck out, word for word and in the same order, under the six documents you keep, so the page closes on you owning the system and hands the method a clean 'so where does it start?'.
motion: Standalone (plays once): the heading rises as it does on every section. The Handover line draws top to bottom, the three capability headings and their brackets draw in, and the six names, tags and old problem lines fade in under six empty dotted places. Meanwhile the six dashed drafts are laid onto a small stack at the left end of the drawing, one at a time, 01 first and 06 on top.

The spread, at about 1.2s (unchanged from round 4): the stack fans out across the Handover line in one row. The top sheet leaves first and the rest follow a beat apart, all taking the same time (1.1s), so no sheet ever passes over another. As each sheet crosses the line its edge turns from dashed to solid and its rough draft becomes the finished page, split exactly at the line. A faint dashed outline is left where the stack stood. The dotted arrow from the stack to the line shows only while the documents cross, then fades. Each sheet's number appears only once it has landed in its own place.

The payoff, in reading order 01 to 06 (unchanged): each document's column lights up for a moment and its edge brightens while its old line is struck out by a drawn line and its new line rises in underneath. Everything has settled by about 4.3s. Nothing loops.

Detail cards (new): once the documents have settled, resting the pointer on a document (its sheet or anything in its column) opens a small card beside it after a short pause (90ms; instant when you move from one document to the next). The card shows the document's number and type, its name, and one line on what it is. Its top line (number, rule, type) sits on exactly the same line as the document's own number and rule, joined to it by a short line, so the card reads as that document's header carried across. The sheet lifts 8px and its edge brightens. The card fades in and rises 4px in 180ms (and fades out in 140ms), lies exactly over the neighbouring sheet, and never covers the document you are on or its old and new lines. Documents 01 to 03 open their card to the right, 04 to 06 to the left. Nothing opens while the documents are still moving, and no card pops up by itself when they settle: if the pointer was already resting on a document, its card opens as soon as the pointer moves.

Keyboard, screen readers and touch (new): each document is now a button, so the row has six tab stops. Tabbing to a document opens its card and draws a 2px ring round the sheet (if you tab in while the documents are still moving, the card opens the moment they settle); Enter or Space opens and closes it; Escape closes it. A screen reader hears 'About Narrative OS', then the card's one line. On a touch screen a tap opens the card, and a second tap, or a tap anywhere else, closes it.

On the live page: the heading and the waiting stack arrive when the section scrolls in. The spread waits until the row of documents is well in view, and at least 1.2s after the section arrived so the heading lands first, then plays once. When the row is already in view on arrival everything has settled about 4.5s later (measured 4.47s), and the cards work from that moment.

With reduced motion, on phones, or if the animation library fails to load, the finished state shows at once and the cards work straight away, appearing and disappearing without animation. On phones each card opens full width over the other document in its pair (the first of a pair opens downward, the second upward), so it never cuts through a row or a heading. With scripts off, the old lines still show struck and hovering or tabbing still shows the cards.
addressed: "I'm not sure why it seems a little bit cluttered. Maybe it's because of too much text happening in the artifact where the animation is happening": I took four pieces of text out of the drawing. The title-block boxes and the handover-test line are gone (see the next two points). The 'Without the system' / 'With the system' labels at the left are gone too: the strike-through and the line under it already say before and after. The three capability headings lost their 'Cap. 01 ·' numbering and now just read 'Narrative systems', 'GTM infrastructure', 'GTM intelligence'. That also stops two sets of numbers (capabilities and documents) stacking on top of each other. The key at the left ('Installed by Kelwin / Owned by you') is smaller and dimmer, and the empty dashed box where the drafts start is drawn in the faintest line. Nothing you approved moved: the heading, the one dark surface, the six documents crossing the Handover line, and under each one its name, type, the old problem struck out and what replaces it. The section is also a little shorter: 941px tall, down from 979px.

"The figure number thing … and those four boxes should be removed": removed completely. The strip of four boxes at the bottom right (the figure number, 'Handover', 'Yours · 06 of 06', 'Specimen') is gone from the page, from the code, and from what screen readers announce. Your standing rules hold for the whole section: no figure numbers or title-block boxes anywhere, and no mention of any other company.

"As well as the handover test thing. It is also unnecessary": removed completely ('The handover test · If it stops working the day we leave, we built it wrong.'). The section now ends on the six new lines, with the usual space before the method.

"When hovering over each of the handover elements, it could maybe display some extra information as an overlay": added. Rest the pointer on any of the six documents, or anywhere in its column, and a small card opens beside it with its number and type, its name, and one line on what it is. The lines are the asset descriptions from round 2, word for word: Narrative OS 'Positioning, language and the message hierarchy every channel inherits.'; Channel Playbooks 'The plays for email, LinkedIn, phone, content, paid and events.'; ICP & Signal Map 'Who to reach, and the live signals that say when.'; Orchestration Rules 'The logic that routes every next-best touch.'; Signal Dashboard 'The readouts your GTM decisions run on.'; Rebuild Sequence 'The prioritised plan, re-scored every quarter.' The card is drawn like the documents themselves: a flat dark panel with one thin border and square corners, and its top line continues the document's own number line, so it looks like part of the drawing rather than a pop-up. It never covers the document you're looking at or its before and after lines. It only works once the documents have finished moving, so it never fights the animation. It also works from the keyboard (Tab to a document, Escape to close) and on touch screens (tap to open, tap again or tap elsewhere to close).
notes: Builder notes, round 5. GENERATED FILE: U.html is generated. Edit scratchpad/redesign/work/handover-U/gen.mjs and run `node work/handover-U/gen.mjs`; don't edit U.html by hand. WHAT CHANGED: (1) removed the caption strip under the drawing (title block and handover-test line) and its CSS, the .is-done stamp step in U.js, and the 104px bottom padding that made room for it; the section now uses the kit's 128px padding top and bottom (941px tall, 979 before). The seam hairline (::after) stays, since method U still has no .ac-sec--ruled. (2) Removed the row captions (.P__rc); each before/after line keeps its screen-reader prefix ('Without the system:' / 'With the system:'). (3) Capability headings: 'Cap. 0n · ' dropped, names kept. (4) Key: 14px (--ac-anno) in --fg-3 with 12px swatches; its first line still sits on the names' baseline. Footprint at rest: --line (was --line-2); during the spread it still steps up to --fg-3. (5) Detail cards. Each sheet's slot is now a <button> (aria-expanded, aria-controls → its card, aria-describedby → the card's line, sr-only name 'About <asset>'); inner wrappers became spans. The card (.P__pop) is the item's last child, absolutely placed: top −8px (flush with the lifted sheet), 16px off the sheet, 260px wide, min-height = sheet + 16px. At that width each card lies exactly over the neighbouring sheet, 8px proud top and bottom, and ends mid-gap before the next one (all six measured, own sheet never overlapped, always inside the section). 01–03 open right, 04–06 (.P__item--l) open left. A 16px leader joins card and sheet; the card's index row (padding-top 7px, 15px row) puts its rule on exactly the sheet's own header rule (sheet y 15–16), so sheet rule → leader → card rule is one line (measured: 0px off at 1440, 0.1px at 1280 zoomed). The name + line sit at the card's foot (flex column, name margin-top auto), so the fixed card height reads as deliberate. Phones: compact card (padding 10/16/12, name padding-top 10px) so an upward card clears the capability heading by ~13px (was ~4px). Type: mono 11px index (--fg) and tag (--fg-3) joined by a hairline (the sheet's own header line, continued), Mona display 20px name (class __pname; renamed from __pn, which collided with sheet 05's dashed-panel path class), 15px body. Panel --panel, 1px --line-2, no shadow, no radius. Open = .is-open on the item (z-index 30, sheet lift 8px, edge inked); in 180ms (opacity + 4px rise), out 140ms. JS: mouse pointerenter opens after 90ms (instant within 400ms of another card), pointerleave closes; keyboard focus opens only when :focus-visible; Enter/Space and touch taps toggle; a mouse click never closes a hover-opened card; Escape and a pointerdown outside close. Nothing opens while .is-deal is on; at hand-back a keyboard-focused sheet opens, while a sheet the mouse merely rests on is armed and opens on the pointer's first move (no uninvited card as the payoff ends). The listeners are bound before the reduced-motion / narrow / no-GSAP early return, so the cards work in every path. Without JS, :hover/:focus-within show the same state (keyed off :not(.is-ink)). The column band is now only the posting cue during the payoff; hover no longer lights it (it merged with the card into one shape). The entrance rule for item children excludes the card (its 'both' fill would otherwise pin it visible). ≤760px: the card spans the whole row (its grid-column is reset so it isn't boxed into the text column); the first of each pair opens down, the second up, so each card lies over its pair-mate and never over a capability heading. TIMING: hand-back is now 0.7s after the last posting cue (no stamp to wait for): standalone ~4.3s; homepage 4.47s after arrival with the row already in view. CHECKS (work/handover-r5/): cards.mjs (hover during the spread stays closed, hand-back opens the hovered sheet, all six cards' bounds, keyboard Tab/Escape/Enter/Space, accessible name 'About Orchestration Rules' + description, touch toggle and tap-outside, reduced motion, phone 390), kskin.mjs (Kelwin skin: every card 152px, names fit, no wrap in the tag row), home.mjs (stitched principle · handover · method at 1440 and 1280, zoomed), nojs.mjs. Strict lint PASS in both skins at 941px; walk of principle S · handover U · method U: no console errors. COPY: unchanged except removals. The card lines are verbatim from round-2 assets X (checked against the live site's AssetInventory.tsx; X's wording is used, e.g. 'prioritised', no Oxford commas, 'next-best' kept on one line). REVIEW PASS (round 5): fixed the 7px misregistration between the card's header rule/leader and the sheet's header rule; renamed the card-name class; hand-back no longer opens a card under a resting pointer; 're-scored' kept on one line in card 06 (the Kelwin skin broke it as 're- / scored'); phone cards made compact. Probes: work/handover-r5/review/probe.mjs, probe2.mjs, probe3.mjs.
